The retrieved hunks show new IR checks for vector main loops, middle blocks, scalar epilogues, and extraction of the last active vector value.

+; CHECK:       [[MIDDLE_BLOCK]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_N:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[N]], [[N_VEC]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IND_ESCAPE:%.*]] = sub i64 [[N_VEC]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_N]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[SCALAR_PH]]
+; CHECK:       [[SCALAR_PH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[BC_RESUME_VAL:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[N_VEC]], %[[MIDDLE_BLOCK]] ], [ 0, %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[BC_RESUME_VAL]], %[[SCALAR_PH]] ], [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i32, ptr [[DST]], i64 [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 0, ptr [[GEP]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add nuw i64 [[IV]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EC]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[EXIT]], !llvm.loop [[LOOP3:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[RET:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[IV]], %[[LOOP]] ], [ [[IND_ESCAPE]], %[[MIDDLE_BLOCK]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[RET]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+

top_candidates.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM change tightens hoist-safety checks by skipping dominated MemorySSA accesses when the candidate instruction is not being sunk. The accompanying test adds cases around hoisting calls that access inaccessible memory, indicating the pass now reasons more carefully about MemorySSA-visible conflicts before moving instructions.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LICM.cpp; MemorySSA; hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a dominance-based filter in LICM's read/write conflict scan over MemorySSA accesses.; Avoids treating dominated accesses as conflicts for non-sink hoisting decisions.; Expands LICM test coverage for inaccessible-memory call hoisting behavior.
Assertion or trace link: Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSA
Reproducer link: Crash occurs during optimizer MemorySSA updating at -O3
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; loop-mssa
Causal explanation: This commit directly changes LICM's interaction with MemorySSA-backed conflict analysis, which is in the same subsystem implicated by the crash. While the hunk does not show the exact failing removal path, it does modify the logic that decides whether a memory access is considered conflicting before hoisting, so it is plausibly related to MemorySSA bookkeeping correctness. The evidence is stronger than for a pure diagnostic change, but still indirect because the retrieved diff does not show the failing assertion site.
Causal confidence: 0.72
Build risk: Touches LICM's MemorySSA-dependent hoist logic; Adds/updates tests for hoisting behavior; Potentially affects -O3 loop optimization correctness and invalidation

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert restores an extra MemorySSA-based guard in LICM store hoisting. The added check prevents hoisting a store past a potentially interfering load when the load's clobbering access is not dominated by the candidate access, addressing a case where the previous clobbering access could be outside the loop even though the load still aliases the store location.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA; LICM; store-hoisting.ll; hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll; call-hoisting.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a dominance check between the candidate memory access and the load's MemorySSA clobbering access before allowing store hoisting.; Strengthens the hoisting invariant from 'clobbering access is outside the loop' to 'no potentially interfering load uses remain that are not dominated in MemorySSA'.; Prevents LICM from moving stores across loads that may still observe the stored location through MemorySSA bookkeeping.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; removeFromLookups; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; MemorySSA.cpp
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; optimizer memory-access bookkeeping; store hoisting / load-before-store interaction
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LICM.cpp; MemorySSA
Causal explanation: The patch changes LICM's MemorySSA-aware hoisting logic to avoid moving a store when a preceding load still has a relevant use/clobber relationship. That is plausibly connected to a MemorySSA bookkeeping crash, because incorrect hoisting can leave MemorySSA uses in an inconsistent state and trigger assertions during removal/update. The test specifically documents a case where the clobbering access is liveOnEntry but the load still aliases the store location, matching the kind of subtle MemorySSA misuse described in the issue.
Causal confidence: 0.84
Build risk: Touches a high-risk scalar optimizer path (LICM) that runs at -O3; Adds a new regression test for store hoisting with MemorySSA; Changes only a local hoisting predicate, so impact is targeted but directly relevant to MemorySSA correctness

@@ -2338,0 +2339,6 @@ static bool noConflictingReadWrites(Instruction *I, MemorySSA *MSSA,
+        // Disable hoisting past potentially interfering loads. Optimized
+        // Uses may point to an access outside the loop, as getClobbering
+        // checks the previous iteration when walking the backedge.
+        // FIXME: More precise: no Uses that alias I.
+        if (!Flags.getIsSink() && !MSSA->dominates(IMD, MU))
+          return false;

@@ -691,0 +692,35 @@ exit:

+@g1 = external global i8

+; preceding load. However, the clobbering memory access for that load is

+entry:

+

+  %v = load i8, ptr %phi
+  store i8 1, ptr @g1
+  br i1 %c, label %loop, label %exit
+
+exit:

+}

behavioral_change: Adds a dominance check between the candidate memory access and the load's MemorySSA clobbering access before allowing store hoisting.
Strengthens the hoisting invariant from 'clobbering access is outside the loop' to 'no potentially interfering load uses remain that are not dominated in MemorySSA'.
Prevents LICM from moving stores across loads that may still observe the stored location through MemorySSA bookkeeping.

assertion_or_trace: Trying to remove memory access that still has uses
reproducer: crash at -O3
optimizer memory-access bookkeeping
store hoisting / load-before-store interaction
issue_link.explanation: The patch changes LICM's MemorySSA-aware hoisting logic to avoid moving a store when a preceding load still has a relevant use/clobber relationship. That is plausibly connected to a MemorySSA bookkeeping crash, because incorrect hoisting can leave MemorySSA uses in an inconsistent state and trigger assertions during removal/update. The test specifically documents a case where the clobbering access is liveOnEntry but the load still aliases the store location, matching the kind of subtle MemorySSA misuse described in the issue.

build_risk: Touches a high-risk scalar optimizer path (LICM) that runs at -O3
Adds a new regression test for store hoisting with MemorySSA
Changes only a local hoisting predicate, so impact is targeted but directly relevant to MemorySSA correctness

top_candidates.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes LICM's hoist-safety logic to ignore MemorySSA accesses that are dominated by the instruction being considered, but only when the operation is not a sink. The accompanying tests show new behavior for hoisting calls involving inaccessible memory and for preserving non-hoist cases when another call reads the same inaccessible memory.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LICM.cpp; MemorySSA; MSSA->dominates; Flags.getIsSink; hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a dominance-based skip in the MemorySSA access scan used by LICM hoist-safety checks.; Refines the conflict test so dominated accesses are not treated as blockers for non-sink hoisting decisions.; Expands LICM tests to cover hoisting of inaccessible-memory calls and non-hoisting when another inaccessible-memory reader is present.
Assertion or trace link: Touches MemorySSA-related LICM logic, which is adjacent to 'MemorySSA::removeFromLookups'; Relevant to optimizer memory-access bookkeeping
Reproducer link: The tests demonstrate changed hoisting behavior for calls involving inaccessible memory, which can alter MemorySSA updates at -O3.; Because the issue is a crash while updating MemorySSA, a LICM change that alters which accesses are considered conflicting is plausibly related.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM / loop-mssa; MemorySSA users in scalar loop optimization
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate among the retrieved hunks because it directly changes LICM's MemorySSA-based conflict analysis. While the patch does not explicitly modify removeFromLookups, it changes the set of accesses LICM treats as conflicting and therefore can affect MemorySSA update paths that are implicated by the crash signature.

Causal explanation: The retrieved hunks do not show any interaction with MemorySSA or with transformations that would directly trigger the reported assertion. top_candidates.subject: [AMDGPU] Use fpext to widen sub DWORD FP printf args (#200870)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This patch changes AMDGPU printf lowering so sub-DWORD floating-point arguments are widened with floating-point extension instead of being bitcast to integers and then sign/zero-extended. It also adjusts the result type construction for vector arguments and updates codegen tests to expect float-preserving widening for half-precision printf operands.
Changed symbols: AMDGPUPrintfRuntimeBindingImpl::lowerPrintfForGpu; AMDGPUPrintfRuntimeBinding; Type::getInt32Ty; IRBuilder::CreateFPExt; IRBuilder::CreateZExt; IRBuilder::CreateSExt
Behavioral change: For FP or FP-vector printf operands whose storage size is smaller than a DWORD, the lowering now uses fpext to widen to float-shaped types instead of integer bitcasts plus integer extension.; The widened result type is derived from the argument type via getWithNewType(Type::getInt32Ty(Ctx)) rather than manually reconstructing vector integer types.
Assertion or trace link: Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSA.cpp

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e98c9074e4f8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -S -passes='default<O3>' %s | FileCheck %s
+
+%pair = type { i64, i64 }
+%quad = type { i64, i64, i64, i64 }
+
+declare void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr noalias writeonly captures(none), ptr noalias readonly captures(none), i64, i1 immarg)
+declare void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr writeonly captures(none), i8, i64, i1 immarg)
+
+; This test verifies that the default O3 pipeline canonicalizes struct allocas
+; to vectors only after memcpyopt has run. The input pattern is:
+;
+;   memcpy tmp, obj, 16
+;   memset obj + 16, 0, 16
+;
+;  ----- SWAP(other, tmp) -----
+;
+;   memcpy swap.tmp, tmp, 16
+;   memcpy tmp, other, 16
+;   memcpy other, swap.tmp, 16
+;
+; It swaps the first 16-bytes of other and tmp, but the first 16-bytes of tmp
+; are the same as the first 16-bytes of obj. This comes from real code from
+; DuckDB, where the swap function is inlined. If struct-to-vector canonicalization
+; runs before memcpyopt, swap.tmp gets promoted to an SSA value and we are stuck
+; saving tmp to swap.tmp. Delaying canonicalization until after memcpyopt lets
+; memcpyopt notice that tmp and obj share the same first 16-bytes, so swap.tmp
+; is no longer needed and the IR collapses to a single load/memmove/store.
+define void @move_then_swap(ptr %dst, ptr %src, ptr %other) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @move_then_swap(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr writeonly captures(none) initializes((0, 16)) [[DST:%.*]], ptr readonly captures(none) [[SRC:%.*]], ptr captures(none) [[OTHER:%.*]]) local_unnamed_addr #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD:%.*]] = load <2 x i64>, ptr [[OTHER]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    tail call void @llvm.memmove.p0.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[OTHER]], ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[SRC]], i64 16, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store <2 x i64> [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD]], ptr [[DST]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  %obj = alloca %quad, align 8
+  %swap.tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %obj, i64 16, i1 false)
+  %obj.tail = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %obj, i64 16
+  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj.tail, i8 0, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %other, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %other, ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -S -passes='default<O3>' %s | FileCheck %s
+
+%pair = type { i64, i64 }
+%quad = type { i64, i64, i64, i64 }
+
+declare void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr noalias writeonly captures(none), ptr noalias readonly captures(none), i64, i1 immarg)
+declare void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr writeonly captures(none), i8, i64, i1 immarg)
+
+; This test verifies that the default O3 pipeline canonicalizes struct allocas
+; to vectors only after memcpyopt has run. The input pattern is:
+;
+;   memcpy tmp, obj, 16
+;   memset obj + 16, 0, 16
+;
+;  ----- SWAP(other, tmp) -----
+;
+;   memcpy swap.tmp, tmp, 16
+;   memcpy tmp, other, 16
+;   memcpy other, swap.tmp, 16
+;
+; It swaps the first 16-bytes of other and tmp, but the first 16-bytes of tmp
+; are the same as the first 16-bytes of obj. This comes from real code from
+; DuckDB, where the swap function is inlined. If struct-to-vector canonicalization
+; runs before memcpyopt, swap.tmp gets promoted to an SSA value and we are stuck
+; saving tmp to swap.tmp. Delaying canonicalization until after memcpyopt lets
+; memcpyopt notice that tmp and obj share the same first 16-bytes, so swap.tmp
+; is no longer needed and the IR collapses to a single load/memmove/store.
+define void @move_then_swap(ptr %dst, ptr %src, ptr %other) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @move_then_swap(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr writeonly captures(none) initializes((0, 16)) [[DST:%.*]], ptr readonly captures(none) [[SRC:%.*]], ptr captures(none) [[OTHER:%.*]]) local_unnamed_addr #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD:%.*]] = load <2 x i64>, ptr [[OTHER]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    tail call void @llvm.memmove.p0.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[OTHER]], ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[SRC]], i64 16, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store <2 x i64> [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD]], ptr [[DST]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  %obj = alloca %quad, align 8
+  %swap.tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %obj, i64 16, i1 false)
+  %obj.tail = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %obj, i64 16
+  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj.tail, i8 0, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %other, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %other, ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.subject: [GVN] MemorySSA for GVN: eliminate redundant loads via MemorySSA (#152859)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds MemorySSA-based load value tracking to GVN, including new reaching-memory-value logic, MemorySSA-aware hoisting decisions, and revised load availability analysis. The patch substantially changes how GVN reasons about memory dependencies when MemorySSA is enabled.
Changed symbols: GVNPass::processLoad; GVNPass::findLoadToHoistIntoPred; GVNPass::AnalyzeLoadAvailability; GVNPass::scanMemoryAccessesUsers; findInvariantGroupValue; maybeLoadStoreLocation; ReachingMemVal; GVNEnableMemorySSA
Behavioral change: Introduces MemorySSA-enabled load processing paths alongside legacy MemDep paths.; Changes hoisting and availability checks to consult MemorySSA clobbers and reaching values.; Adds logic to scan users of MemoryAccess nodes and derive clobber/def information from MemorySSA.; Modifies offset handling and dependency classification for load PRE under MemorySSA.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; memory access; clobberingMemoryAccess; load PRE; reaching memory values
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O3 crash while updating MemorySSA; this commit changes a major optimizer user of MemorySSA.; The patch alters load-hoisting and dependency bookkeeping, which can affect memory-access use/def chains.
Pass or subsystem link: Scalar/GVN; MemorySSA integration; load PRE / hoisting
Causal explanation: This commit is strongly related to the issue context because it introduces and expands MemorySSA usage in GVN, a high-risk optimizer subsystem for MemorySSA bookkeeping bugs. Summary: This commit adds LoopVectorize test coverage for early-exit loops with stores under masking and tail-folding, including cases with uncountable exits and scalarized conditional operations. The retrieved hunks are entirely test-only and describe expected vectorized control flow, masked loads/stores, and scalar epilog handling for loops that may exit early while still performing memory writes.

causal_evidence.summary: This patch changes SLP vectorizer test expectations so that several scalar intrinsic call sequences are recognized and emitted as vector intrinsic calls instead of per-lane extract/call/insertelement chains. The retrieved hunks are entirely in SLPVectorizer tests for NVPTX, X86, and AArch64, covering ctlz, powi, sin, and atan2 vector-library mappings, including poison-aware insertion patterns.
behavioral_change: Vectorizes scalar intrinsic call patterns into vector intrinsic calls when a vector library mapping is available.
Replaces lane-by-lane extract/call/insertelement lowering with shufflevector-based packing and a single vector intrinsic call.
Adjusts poison-handling expectations for vectorized intrinsic formation in tests.

reproducer: No direct crash-reproducer behavior is shown in the retrieved hunks; only SLP vectorization codegen/test expectations are changed.

top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] Fold X == Identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) (#202748)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change teaches InstCombine's simplification logic to fold min/max intrinsics when one operand is replaced by the intrinsic's identity element, while preserving poison-related flags by refusing to fold unless flags can be dropped. The visible patch adds a new `simplifyWithOpsReplaced` case for `MinMaxIntrinsic` and expands InstCombine tests for signed/unsigned min/max select patterns.
Changed symbols: simplifyWithOpsReplaced; MinMaxIntrinsic; InstructionSimplify; llvm.smin; llvm.umin; llvm.smax; llvm.umax
Behavioral change: Adds identity-based folding for min/max intrinsics after operand replacement.; Preserves correctness by checking poison-generating annotations and requiring flag dropping when needed.; Enables more aggressive simplification of select/min-max patterns in InstCombine.
Assertion or trace link: No direct match to `Trying to remove memory access that still has uses`; No direct match to `MemorySSA::removeFromLookups`; No direct match to `MemorySSA.cpp`
Reproducer link: The tests are about InstCombine folding of min/max/select patterns, not a MemorySSA crash; No evidence here of a failing `-O3` MemorySSA update path
Pass or subsystem link: InstructionSimplify; InstCombine

index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f

@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit generalizes SimpleLoopUnswitch's notion of trivial unswitching and adjusts phase-ordering tests accordingly. The visible hunks show new or updated expectations for loop unswitching and loop-guard handling, including cold-function and PGO-related cases, but no direct MemorySSA implementation changes.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(

+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;

+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0

diff --git a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
index d09def0afdb7..6e56dfd783d1 100644
--- a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
+++ b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
@@ -494,0 +495,25 @@ endfunction()
+# PluginManager discovers dynamic script interpreter plugins at runtime by
+# scanning the directory that holds liblldb, so a plugin is loaded only when it
+# sits beside it. A framework build moves liblldb into the bundle, so the plugin
+# must move with it and carry an rpath that reaches liblldb from its new
+# location.
+function(lldb_add_scriptinterpreter_plugin_to_framework name)
+  if(NOT LLDB_BUILD_FRAMEWORK)
+    return()
+  endif()
+  set_property(TARGET ${name} APPEND PROPERTY
+    INSTALL_RPATH "@loader_path/../../..")
+  # Copy under the unversioned name: PluginManager derives a plugin's
+  # initializer symbol from it. A versioned copy would load but never
+  # initialize.
+  set(plugin_in_framework
+    "${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_ABSOLUTE_BUILD_DIR}/LLDB.framework/Versions/${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_VERSION}/$<TARGET_LINKER_FILE_NAME:${name}>")
+  add_custom_command(TARGET ${name} POST_BUILD VERBATIM
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy "$<TARGET_FILE:${name}>" "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Copy ${name} into LLDB.framework")
+  add_custom_target(${name}-framework-cleanup
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E remove "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Removing ${name} from LLDB.framework")
+  add_dependencies(lldb-framework-cleanup ${name}-framework-cleanup)
+endfunction()
+

# Returns TRUE in `out_var` if any of `libs` is `liblldb` or already carries
# the LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB property.
function(_lldb_links_liblldb_check out_var libs)
  set(${out_var} FALSE PARENT_SCOPE)
  foreach(lib ${libs})
    if("${lib}" STREQUAL "liblldb")
      set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
      return()
    endif()
    if(TARGET "${lib}")
      get_target_property(_p "${lib}" LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB)
      if(_p)
        set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
        return()
      endif()
    endif()
  endforeach()
endfunction()

function(_lldb_propagate_links_liblldb name libs)
  _lldb_links_liblldb_check(_links_liblldb "${libs}")
  set_target_properties(${name} PROPERTIES LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB ${_links_liblldb})
endfunction()

# Records a target's undefined LLDB symbols for re-export by liblldb.
# The output path is appended to the LLDB_DYNAMIC_SCRIPTINTERPRETER_SYMBOL_FILES
# global property.
function(lldb_record_dynamic_script_interpreter_exports target)
  set(symbol_file
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}.undefined.symbols")

  # llvm-nm is registered as a CMake target after the LLDB subdirectory is
  # processed, so a forward target reference is required. LLVM_NM, when set,
  # points to a prebuilt host tool for cross-compiled builds.
  if(LLVM_NM)
    set(nm_exe "${LLVM_NM}")
    set(nm_dep)
  else()
    set(nm_exe "$<TARGET_FILE:llvm-nm>")
    set(nm_dep llvm-nm)
  endif()

  set(extra_args)
  if(APPLE)
    list(APPEND extra_args --mach-o)
  endif()

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT ${symbol_file}
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      ${LLDB_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/extract-dynamic-script-interpreter-exports.py
      --nm ${nm_exe}
      ${extra_args}
      -o ${symbol_file}
      $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${target}>
    DEPENDS
      ${LLDB_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/extract-dynamic-script-interpreter-exports.py
      $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${target}>
      ${nm_dep}
    COMMAND_EXPAND_LISTS
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "Extracting LLDB symbols required by ${target}"
  )

  add_custom_target(${target}-exports DEPENDS ${symbol_file})
  set_target_properties(${target}-exports PROPERTIES FOLDER "LLDB/API")

  set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PR

diff --git a/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp b/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp
index fa0ab712fa64..1cbf3bd63363 100644
--- a/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp
+++ b/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp
@@ -102,0 +103,13 @@ void buildGPUPassPipeline(OpPassManager &pm,
+  // Break down high-level micro-scaling (MX) ops (arith.scaling_extf and
+  // arith.scaling_truncf) into standard arith ops (extf/truncf + mulf), and
+  // expand extf/truncf on f8E8M0FNU into integer bit manipulation. This runs
+  // before the XeVM/LLVM conversions. The f4E2M1FN expansion patterns are
+  // intentionally left disabled: f4E2M1FN extf/truncf are lowered by the XeVM
+  // conversions (xevm.extf), whereas f8E8M0FNU is not supported there and so
+  // must be expanded here.
+  {
+    arith::ArithExpandOpsPassOptions arithExpandOptions;
+    arithExpandOptions.includeF8E8M0 = true;
+    pm.addNestedPass<gpu::GPUModuleOp>(
+        arith::createArithExpandOpsPass(arithExpandOptions));
+  }
